purpose: Machine-readable 1943-10-01 surface-combatant capability and survival guard. It converts existing class/design/doctrine canon into runtime constraints without inventing exact event-local availability.
principles: Hull survival, availability, readiness, assignment and combat capability are separate clocks.
Do not substitute historical loss dates for branch-authoritative survival evidence.
Do not score a ship only by nominal caliber/displacement; use practical speed, reliability, fire-control, torpedo cycle, damage-state continuity and formation role.
Working relative bands are task-specific sensitivity anchors, never universal fleet multipliers.
Exact individual-hull readiness at an event remains runtime input unless an authoritative settlement fixes it.

survival_anchors.rule: Four Kongo-class hulls survive into the 1943 branch. Hiei/Kirishima have June-Efate activity and Haruna May-Aleutians activity; historical Guadalcanal loss dates are forbidden defaults.

Kongo_class.role: 30-knot-class fast battleship formation; carrier support, fast surface interception, cruiser/DD counterforce, reserve/raiding options
Kongo_class.capability: Primary branch gain is repeatable practical speed, machinery reliability, formation schedule robustness and state-transition resilience, not new-battleship armor.
limits: Basic armor/waterline protection remains a major limiter against modern battleship gunfire.
No automatic commitment merely because four hulls survive.

Yamato_class.role: strategic reserve/main battle force; enemy battleship fixation, landing-force breakthrough or major surface strike only when geometry/air cover/fuel justify it
Yamato_class.capability: 46cm main battery and 27kt-class concept retained; branch gain is reliability, damage localization, steering/power/firefighting integration and confidence in sustained planned performance.
Yamato_class.speed_anchor: 27kt-class practical planned speed; favorable trials may be ~27.6-27.8kt but this is not a universal tactical-speed bonus.
limits: Do not model improvement as armor multiplier.
1943 Efate/Midway branch evidence favors strategic-reserve use under hostile air conditions.

Ise_Hyuga.state: battleships; no aviation-battleship conversion in current branch
Ise_Hyuga.role: second-line battleship, base/convoy/landing support, reserve and test/training duties; frees fast battleships for forward use
Ise_Hyuga.speed_anchor: ~25kt class; do not mix into fast-carrier screen by default

Mogami_class.survival: Four hulls survive the branch MI collision/loss divergence; repaired-hull local availability is event-specific.
Mogami_class.role: night surface force / cruiser interception / torpedo threat / continued gun action after moderate damage
limits: Do not assume all four simultaneously mission-ready without local OOB/readiness.

Asashio_class.role: fleet torpedo/night action and escort; improved stability/reliability rather than large universal speed jump

Kagero_Yugumo_line.role: mature high-speed fleet torpedo/escort system; Yugumo is maturation/standardization, not a radically faster class

Shimakaze.state: 1943 branch service use permitted when local OOB/readiness confirms
Shimakaze.role: high-speed torpedo combat; individual mission assignment remains event-local

surface_gunfire.effect: By 1942, better calculation/calibration/optics/I-O can shorten effective-solution convergence ~5-10%; normal daylight hit probability working change +2-5% relative under applicable equipment/training.
surface_gunfire.rule: No generic 20-40% hit bonus; preserve weather, visibility, maneuver, radar and crew effects.

torpedo_cycle.effect: Mature equipped Japanese cruiser/DD units can sometimes convert carried reloads into a second effective salvo roughly 12-20 minutes after first launch under suitable conditions.
torpedo_cycle.rule: Reload torpedoes are not instantaneous doubled first-salvo firepower; resolve 0/partial/full second-salvo availability by combat time, maneuver and damage.

speed_reliability.effect: Improvement often appears as probability of making planned speed under load/fouling/fatigue, affecting interception, withdrawal and re-entry thresholds.

damage_control.effect: Reinvested weight/power/structural margin can reduce transition from moderate damage to mission kill and preserve selected functions after non-catastrophic hits.
damage_control.rule: No double count as both generic survival and firing-continuity multipliers.

radar_optical_integration.rule: US radar early-contact advantage remains important, especially at night/poor visibility. Japanese optical/torpedo follow-up can be strong after contact, but early warning and fire-control stages are separate.

allied_runtime_rule.United_States: Use branch OOB/survival first. US surface forces avoided some historical Guadalcanal attrition, but exact hull presence/readiness must be event-local. Historical hardware/doctrine may be fallback only where branch evidence does not diverge.
allied_runtime_rule.Britain: Use branch Eastern Fleet losses/allocation and event-local availability; do not infer a historically scheduled surface response without paid shipping, air cover, maintenance and command conditions.
